title: A generic Stack[T]
prompt:
Implement `Stack(Generic[T])` with `push(item: T)`, `pop() -> T` (IndexError on empty), `peek() -> T` (IndexError on empty), and `__len__`. Also implement `first(xs: List[T]) -> T` raising `ValueError('empty sequence')` on an empty list.

Runtime must behave exactly like the untyped version — the generic parameter is a design contract (your annotations must reference T where relevant).
boilerplate:
from typing import TypeVar, Generic, List

T = TypeVar('T')

# TODO: Stack and first

tests.name: stack behaves and preserves values
tests.code:
s = Stack()
s.push(1)
s.push('a')
assert len(s) == 2
assert s.pop() == 'a'
assert s.peek() == 1
assert s.pop() == 1
try:
    Stack().pop()
except IndexError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('empty pop must raise IndexError')
print('ok')
tests.hint: Store items in a list; the annotations document the contract (item: T, pop() -> T).

tests.name: first() and runtime subscript
tests.code:
assert first([3, 1, 2]) == 3
assert first(['x', 'y']) == 'x'
try:
    first([])
except ValueError:
    pass
else:
    raise AssertionError('first([]) must raise ValueError')
sub = Stack[int]()
assert isinstance(sub, Stack), 'Generic classes support runtime subscription'
print('ok')
tests.hint: Raise ValueError with the exact message for empty input; Stack[int]() must work at runtime via Generic.
